# WM DSGVO Privacy Eraser

> WordPress plugin for Art. 17 DSGVO erasure requests: a public form records a request and mails a single-use link to a page whose button confirms it; after confirmation it anonymises that address's comments, deletes its non-administrator account, optionally anonymises WooCommerce billing fields, and adds an HMAC-chained erasure record. It does not export data, does not reach other plugins' tables and makes no legal assessment of a request.

## Overview


- Shortcode: `[wm_dsgvo_erasure_portal]` and compiled Gutenberg block `wm/dsgvo-erasure-portal`
- Ecosystem bridges: WP 6.5+ Block Bindings `wm-dsgvo-eraser/status`, GenerateBlocks 2.x Dynamic Tag `{{wm_eraser_status}}`, actions `wm_eraser_ready` and `wm_eraser_completed`, filters `wm_eraser_anonymize_personal_data`, `wm_eraser_rest_rate_limit`, `wm_eraser_status_text`
- REST: `wm-dsgvo-eraser/v1` — `POST /request` (blinded-IP rate-limited), `GET /confirm` (302 redirect to confirmation page), `GET /verify` (`manage_options`)
- Confirmation page: `/?wm_dsgvo_erasure=confirm&wm_erasure_request=…&wm_erasure_token=…` (GET shows the button, POST erases)
- WP-CLI: `wp dsgvo erase <email>`, `wp dsgvo verify`
- Storage: `wp_wm_dsgvo_requests`, `wp_wm_dsgvo_erasure_certificates`, options `wm_dsgvo_cert_chain_tip`, `wm_dsgvo_schema_version`, `wm_dsgvo_anonymize_wc_orders`, `wm_dsgvo_eraser_delete_data_on_uninstall` (opt-in uninstall)
- Documentation measured against the code: README.md, DEVELOPERS.md
- Version 1.4.2.

## Standards

- PHP 8.2+ with libsodium, strict types, WordPress coding style (tabs); no phpcs run in CI
- Self-hosted assets in `/assets/`
- Prepared SQL, constant-time token comparison, keyed hashes for addresses and IPs
